name: 4x4 tower six bricks tall red top
description: 4x4 footprint tower, six bricks tall (6 layers × 24 LDU = 144 LDU). Each layer is two 2x4 bricks (3001) placed side by side along Z at z=-20 and z=+20. Bottom 5 layers in dark bluish grey (72), top layer in red (4). The two vertical columns are not laterally connected but are held together by stacking — a valid simple tower build.
verdict: FAIL - fix misaligned_parts first, then fragmented_submodels.

name: minifigure with hair
description: Standard LEGO minifigure assembled from official parts: red legs (3816/3817), red hips (3815b), red torso (973), yellow head (3626cp01), black classic male hair (3901), yellow arms (3818/3819), and yellow hands (3820). Hair placed at y=-65 to sit low on the head stud. All connections use minifig-specific joints (neck stud, clip pegs, hand clips) rather than standard brick studs.
verdict: PASS - every part is on the stud grid.

name: Blue police officer minifigure
description: A blue police officer minifigure with two swords, one held in each hand. The build relies on the standard minifigure torso, legs, and head assembly, with the arms positioned at a slight outward angle to accommodate the sword hilts, which are attached to the hands via the 3820.dat pieces. The two 3847.dat swords are placed symmetrically, angled outward and downward from the hands, so the figure reads clearly as armed and ready for action
verdict: PASS - every part is on the stud grid and nothing overlaps.

name: Gnarled moss bonsai
description: Gnarled moss bonsai is a compact, low-part-count model of a bonsai tree in a shallow blue pot, built from alternating stacked 3941.dat cylinders to form a tapering trunk and a separate supporting branch that rises to a wide flat canopy. The canopy is a 3028.dat plate covered with 54200.dat cheese slopes arranged in a grid to suggest moss tufts, while the soil is a single 3795.dat plate set atop the pot base. Useful as a starting point for any small decorative tree, topiary, or alien plant that needs a sturdy trunk and canopy silhouette without detailed branching, since the repeating cylinder stack and slope grid are easily swapped for other shapes
verdict: PASS - every part is on the stud grid and nothing overlaps.

name: Simple oak tree with blossom
description: Simple oak tree with blossom: a small display tree with a four-stud square trunk and a roughly spherical crown, useful as a starting point for dioramas, bases, or landscape vignettes. The trunk stacks four 1x1 bricks on a root flare of five side-by-side 1x2 plates, and the crown is built from eleven 2x2 round bricks arranged in two cross-shaped rings around a central brick, all seated on squared base plates; the blossom is suggested by five studs on the top ring. Height is about 23 studs, and the crown width spans 7 studs
verdict: PASS - every part is on the stud grid, nothing overlaps.
